# Five practical running guides — editorial and release notes

These pages implement the five-topic shortlist selected from Ubersuggest US / English
research on 24 October 2026. Estimates retrieved then: treadmill pace chart 9,900 / SD 19;
how long does it take to train for a marathon 3,600 / SD 11; run walk marathon
170 / SD 16; marathon taper 720 / SD 29; strength training for marathon runners
1,600 / SD 36. Search estimates are research context, not public-page claims or
traffic forecasts. Actual results included established publishers and AI answer
features; low reported difficulty is not evidence of an easy ranking.

## What each page adds

- Treadmill: four-way speed/pace converter, original 21-row metric/imperial table,
  printable one-page reference, whole-session arithmetic and incline limitations.
- Duration: 12/16/20-week calendar comparison using UTC date arithmetic; workload
  comparison against the opening weeks of a plan; original hypothetical time budget.
- Run-walk: complete and partial interval examples, stop accounting and direct
  handoff to the existing tested calculator. No second competing calculator.
- Taper: adjustable distance budgets, distinction between percent remaining and
  percent removed, separate race distance and a daily example whose total adds up.
- Strength: two timed exercise sheets with alternatives, sets, repetitions, rest,
  progression, running-week placement and printable records.

## Authorship and evidence

Davin Pinto's established site biography identifies him as a recreational runner
and site creator. No coaching qualification, clinical review, independent reviewer,
new personal result or hands-on field test has been added. Existing first-person
experience is linked to the published Sydney/rebuild accounts and attributed.
New runner cases, schedules and calculations are explicitly illustrative. The
existing editorial policy discloses assistance from software including AI.

Primary sources consulted during 24–25 October 2026:

1. NIST Guide to the SI Appendix B.9 — international mile = 1.609344 km.
2. Jones & Doust 1996, PMID 8887211 — the scope of the 1% treadmill experiment.
3. TCS London Marathon official training-plans page — 16-week plans, not copied schedules.
4. B.A.A. official Boston Marathon training page — 20-week framework and the
   approximately 25 miles/week Level One starting workload; schedules not reproduced.
5. Hottenrott et al. 2016, PMID 25467199 — small run-walk/continuous comparison;
   no general cardiac-protection or injury-prevention claim.
6. Bosquet et al. 2007, PMID 17762369 — competitive-athlete taper meta-analysis;
   sport/individual applicability is qualified.
7. Smyth & Lawlor 2021, PMID 34651125 — observational recreational marathon taper
   evidence; no causal individual time-saving promise.
8. Llanos-Lagos et al. 2024, PMID 38165636 — running economy and strength methods;
   introductory examples do not claim to reproduce high-load study protocols.
9. Currier et al. 2026, PMID 41843416 — updated ACSM healthy-adult resistance guidance.
10. Wu et al. 2024, PMID 38261240 — injury prevention is a distinct and uncertain outcome.

Links appear beside claims and in each page's source list. Original arithmetic is
described in `/methodology/` with matching anchors. New Article metadata points to
the real author page and original social cards, with accurate publication dates.
No expert-review, HowTo eligibility or FAQ rich-result claims are made.

## Discovery and maintenance

Each page is linked from the blog index and HTML/XML sitemaps. Nine existing
contextual locations link to the relevant new resources: the training planner,
pace calculator, chart-use guide, five-hour goal guide, pace-workout guide,
readiness guide, disrupted-plan guide, long-run guide and weight-loss guide.
The new articles also link to relevant established tools and one another.

No production dependency, advert loader, affiliate destination or consent/analytics
change is introduced. Existing goal controls, calculator algorithms, redirects,
pace-band orientation and print output remain covered by regression suites.

This content addresses five distinct reader tasks. It cannot guarantee AdSense
approval, search rankings, an injury-free build or a particular race performance.
